To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the clustering estimates for the unbounded spin system are obtained for the first time, (ii) the results are applicable to the Bosonic case, (iii) they are valid in a large range of the coupling parameter, (iv) the results are valid also for small self-interaction, (v) the results are obtained for a large class of unbounded spin systems, including the case of the quantum field theory.

(i) the truncated correlations of a spin system with unbounded spin variables, with a general class of interaction kernels satisfying the usual decay assumptions, satisfy clustering estimates, and (ii) in the near massive case, these clustering estimates can be made quantitative, and in particular, the correlation length is bounded

(i) the clustering bounds on truncated correlations for an unbounded spin model with a large mass are of the same order as the corresponding bounds for the Gaussian free field; (ii) for an unbounded interacting spin model with a finite mass, the clustering bounds on the truncated correlations are of the same quality as those for the Gaussian free fields, provided the self-interaction is sufficiently large.
